children: New York-based software startup Clay, which was co-founded by an Egyptian entrepreneur, has secured $115 million, bringing the company’s valuation to $7.1 billion

The Series D funding was led by US-headquartered Wellington Management, with participation from Sequoia Capital, StepStone Group, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Perennial, Meritech Capital, DST Global, CapitalG, BoxGroup, Boldstart Ventures, Bloomberg Beta and Evolution Media Capital.
The artificial intelligence (AI) sales tool provider was co-founded in 2017 by Egypt-born Kareem Amin and Canadian Nicolae Rusan.
It caters to more than 17,000 customers, including 80% of the Forbes AI 50 and major AI labs like Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.
(Writing by Cleofe Maceda; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Egyptian-led software startup Clay raises $115mln at $7.1bln valuation
